It is not refused, which goes against the restore's 'never reuse' text: a plain run starts a fresh cutover under the reused tag; '--from-phase g' prints point-1 advice including '--date X --from-phase d', and that path then dies at point 1 in final_backup (no gate_backup_file). Fail-safe; Minor P5-F10. If the restore was not archived, the NOT_MERGED + merge.done row dies 'use a NEW --date'. (5) Fresh cutover with a new --date after a restore: PRE, cross-tag guard skips *.restored-*, phase a/c record and tag the running OLD image (which the restore redeployed), and a fresh final dump is taken in the new stop window. With an unarchived merged dir, the cross-tag guard dies. Point-2 restore point: within the merge's own --date dir it is always the pre-merge final dump from the merge's stop window (P5-F1/F5/F6 guards unchanged). Across dirs it is correct only when the wrong --date dir has no final_backup_file (P5-F9).
checks.retry2_db_signal_vs_t7_t8: MATCHES. migrated_to_id IS NOT NULL on any row is exactly 'merge committed'. Written only by the one UPDATE inside the gated copy DO block, after the gate RETURN (work_item_merge.enabled <> 'on') and the run-once RETURN, inside applySchema's single BEGIN/COMMIT together with the T8 parity and guard blocks, so a rolled-back run leaves every row NULL and a committed run sets every pending row (key_number is NOT NULL, so the wim_map join covers all of them, and T8 parity aborts otherwise). Partial state: after commit the T8 trigger (same EXISTS ... IS NOT NULL condition, created in the same transaction) blocks new tracker inserts, so new NULL rows cannot appear; even if they did, 'any NOT NULL' still reads MERGED, which is correct. Run-once guard: a second gated run is a no-op and leaves the column as is. Gate-off migrate at normal container start returns before the UPDATE, so it never sets the column, and the expand step only ADDs it. No app code writes it. Restore: the final dump is taken in phase e before merge_started, refuse_if_merge_started and the DB-first policy prevent any post-merge final dump, and production already has the column (checklist Phase A row), so a restored DB reads NOT_MERGED with no trigger and NOCOL cannot fire falsely. EMPTY needs zero tracker rows; production has 180, and nothing in the server hard-deletes tracker_items outside tests, so the marker fallback is not reachable in production. The NOT_MERGED + merge_started row stays IN-FLIGHT (point 2) on purpose: after an ssh 255 the remote migrate may still commit.
checks.retry2_contracts_and_order: PASS (unchanged). Snapshot/verify argv, the /cutover bind mount, the snapshot path, MERGE_CMD and validate_merge_output are unchanged in substance. T16<->T17: exit 0/1/2, verify in phase g under POINT 2. T17<->T7/T8 notices: rc 0, last line 'Schema applied.', at least one 'work-item-merge: workspace=' line, no 'copy skipped' line. Order: final dump (phase e, after the stop) -> assert_final_dump_fresh -> snapshot -> merge_started -> merge -> merge.done -> ANALYZE (phase f) -> verify (phase g). check_date_policy, then the FINAL_BACKUP_FILE read, then enforce_resume_policy (DB first) all run before the phase loop. P5-F1, P5-F5 and P5-F6 remain resolved: the freshness guard, refuse_if_merge_started and the per-dir policy cases all pass in the 138-check self-check.
checks.retry2_dry_run: PASS. Zero remote calls in every mode tried (calls.log 0 bytes). The DB read runs only in --execute: db_merge_state is reached only through compute_merge_state, which enforce_resume_policy calls after its EXECUTE=1 check. check_date_policy returns immediately when EXECUTE=0.
checks.recovery_confirm_p5f9: RESOLVED in logic (fake-remote harness, check_date_policy patched in a scratch copy only to reach compute_merge_state). compute_merge_state clears FINAL_BACKUP_FILE first and the early load in main is gone, so main's in-loop reload only runs after the policy passes. In the MERGED + no merge.done here branch, the printed restore names only the final dump of the single dir that holds the merge markers (other tag), or this dir's dump when this dir alone holds merge_started (wording: committed but never recorded, do not resume), or the placeholder for zero or several marker dirs. Across every scenario the printed restore never named a dump outside the marker dir, which meets spec Appendix B.6 and the Rollback Plan. POST, IN-FLIGHT and PRE still take the dump from this --date dir, which is the marker dir in those states. Masked in the real script by P5-F11: unpatched, every scenario aborts earlier in check_date_policy (fail-closed). Cosmetic only: print_recovery's 'Check the merge state FIRST (is <this --date dir>/merge.done present?)' line still names the --date dir, while the die text above it names the right dir.
checks.recovery_confirm_p5f10: Refusal logic implemented and self-checked (P5-F10 case, stubbed rout), and in the patched harness it refuses every reuse of an archived --date and allows a new one. The remote ls string it relies on fails on every host without a matching archive, so as written it refuses every --execute run (P5-F11).
checks.recovery_confirm_regressions: P5-F1/F5/F6/F7/F8 stay resolved in logic. The DB-authoritative state is unchanged apart from table_schema='public': migrated_to_id IS NOT NULL = MERGED still matches the T7/T8 commit semantics. T16<->T17: the snapshot/verify argv, /cutover bind mount, snapshot path and exit 0/1/2 are unchanged, with verify in phase g under POINT 2. Notices: validate_merge_output is unchanged (rc 0, last line 'Schema applied.', at least one 'work-item-merge: workspace=' line, no 'copy skipped' line). Order is unchanged: final dump (phase e) -> assert_final_dump_fresh -> snapshot -> merge_started -> merge -> merge.done -> ANALYZE (phase f) -> verify (phase g). Dry-run makes zero remote calls in every mode (calls.log 0 bytes). Reachability caveat: in --execute every path stops in check_date_policy before reaching any of this (P5-F11).

findings.description: The restore point is older than the merge input. Phase b takes and verifies the pg_dump while the site is still live. Maintenance and the server stop only happen in phase e, and phase d sits in between (local client build, docker build, image save, scp, docker load), so the gap can be many minutes. The snapshot and the merge in phase f include every write from that window, but the backup used by restore-ggf.sh does not, so a failure-point-2 restore silently drops writes the operator assumes are safe. This contradicts spec Appendix B.6 ('no old-image writes between backup and cutover because the server is down') and understates the loss described in the Rollback Plan and checklist line 99 ('edits since the merge/reopening are lost'). The ordering comes from the T17 packet itself (backup before maintenance), so a per-task audit judged against that packet could not see the conflict with the spec. This is distinct from T17's carried Minor about live row-count drift causing false aborts.
findings.fix: After the phase-e stop and before phase f, take a final pg_dump -Fc, run pg_restore --list on it, and optionally repeat the scratch-restore count check. With the server stopped, live counts are stable, which also clears the carried row-count drift Minor. Record this dump as backup_file/BACKUP_FILE so print_recovery and restore-ggf.sh use it. Keep phase b as the early restorability gate that aborts before any change. Update the checklist step list and the failure-point-2 wording to match.
findings.defer_note: The fix goes into git-ignored host files, so it cannot be a correction commit. It must land and be rehearsed in T18. It blocks T19.
findings.resolution: Resolved for every pre-merge path (cycle 4, content-hash audited): first run, retry --from-phase d, plain resume, --from-phase f after a failed or superseded final dump, and manual restart then stop. The phase f freshness guard (marker, generation, file, flag, container identity) closes them. The post-merge re-run through phase e can still replace the restore point; tracked as P5-F6.

findings.description: The cutover enables the merge only through the env path: WORK_ITEM_MERGE=on -> migrate() -> applySchema(client) with no option -> SET LOCAL work_item_merge.enabled. Every merged-schema test (T7, T8, T13, T16) enables it with applySchema({workItemMerge:true}), and the env var is only ever stubbed to an empty string. migrate.test.ts uses a fake client whose fixture prints both 'copy skipped' and a 'workspace=' summary, the exact combination T17's validator rejects, so it says nothing about real gate behaviour. A regression in the env comparison would only surface at cutover, where it would hit failure point 2 after commit: the expand-only schema commits with rc 0, and the validator then fails on 'copy skipped'.
findings.fix: Add an integration test (RUN_INTEGRATION) that points the pool at a scratch schema, seeds tracker rows, sets vi.stubEnv('WORK_ITEM_MERGE','on'), calls migrate(), and captures console.log. It should assert the four validate_merge_output conditions: no throw, last line 'Schema applied.', at least one 'work-item-merge: workspace=' line, and no 'copy skipped' line. A unit assertion in migrate.test.ts that the env var causes the SET LOCAL query to run before the merge SQL is a cheaper partial alternative.

findings.description: restore-ggf.sh leaves cutover-state/<date>/ untouched (phase-a..f.done, merge_started.done, merge.done, analyze.done). If the operator retries the cutover with the same --date after a point-2 restore, phases a-f are skipped and phase f prints 'merge already committed'. Phase g then starts the new image on the restored, unmerged database (the entrypoint migrate is gate-off), and verify against the old snapshot fails, so the run loops into point 2 again. The behaviour is fail-safe, but neither script nor the checklist describes how to retry after a restore.
findings.fix: At the end of restore-ggf.sh, move cutover-state/<date> aside (for example to cutover-state/<date>.restored-<stamp>), or print an explicit instruction to retry with a new --date. Add a 'Retry after restore' line to the checklist's failure handling.

findings.note_retry1: Interaction with P5-F7: after a point-2 restore, cutover-state/<date>/ still says POST. A same-date '--from-phase d' now dies at point 2 and prints restore-ggf.sh for the original final dump; following that would drop the writes made since the restore reopened the site. Advice to 'retry with a new --date' is correct only after a restore; in an unrestored POST state it is exactly the P5-F7 trap. Fix both together.
findings.note_retry2: Partly addressed: restore-ggf.sh now archives cutover-state/<date> as <date>.restored-<ts> after health passes, writes a 'restored' record and prints 'retry with a NEW --date'. The checklist describes this. Reuse of the archived --date is still not refused (P5-F10). The rest stays deferred to T18.

findings.description: Verify can fail on data the merge migration legitimately changes or on preconditions the snapshot never asserts. (a) The new schema.sql key backfill ($board_tracker_key_backfill) runs inside the merge transaction and assigns keys to live board cards with a NULL key_number. The snapshot excludes those cards from keys, but listMergedWorkItems includes them afterwards. (b) Live cards with column_id NULL before the merge are excluded from every snapshot metric but appear afterwards as source='tracker'. (c) selectBoardWorkItemRows/selectWorkItemRows inner-join status, whereas the snapshot and the real GET /board handler (leftJoin) do not, so a NULL status_id card would drop out of verify only. Production meets all three preconditions today (the Phase A checklist shows 0 live NULL keys, the old image never writes column-less cards, and cards.status_id is NOT NULL once backfilled). However, a violation is only detected after the commit, which makes it a point-2 full restore instead of a cheap point-1 abort.
findings.fix: In `snapshot` mode, fail closed before the merge: exit 1, which phase f maps to a pre-merge abort. Do this if any live board card has key_number NULL or status_id NULL, if any live card has column_id NULL, or if any tracker_items row already has migrated_to_id set. Alternatively, align verify's board read with the GET /board join. Have T18 record these precondition counts on the production copy.

findings.description: This is the residual of P5-F1. The stop-generation check exists only inside final_backup (phase e). Phase f checks only that camel-server is not running right now, so a restore can still be older than the merge input on three paths that documented flags reach. (1) The final dump fails in phase e (point 1), and the operator resumes with --from-phase f. Phases a-e are skipped, final_backup_file was never written and FINAL_BACKUP_FILE stays empty. The server is stopped, so the guard passes and the snapshot and merge run. At point 2 print_recovery shows only a placeholder, and the only dump on disk is the gate dump, which restore-ggf.sh refuses. (2) On a retry, the supersede step succeeds (the old dump is renamed and final_backup.done removed) but the fresh pg_dump fails. vars still names the old path, which no longer exists. With --from-phase f the merge runs, the point-2 restore fails 'test -s', and only the stale .superseded-* file is left. (3) After a point-1 recovery the site reopens and takes writes. The operator then stops the server manually and resumes, either plainly or with --from-phase f. The guard passes, stop_gen is unchanged, and the pre-reopen dump becomes the restore point, which is the exact P5-F1 bug class. Also: restore-ggf.sh refuses the gate dump but accepts a *.superseded-* dump, which is stale by construction. Paths (1) and (2) go against the printed advice (retry --from-phase d), but the checklist runbook header documents --from-phase <a-h> as a general resume mode, and the bar is 'any path'.
findings.fix: In phase f, when merge.done is absent and before the snapshot, require all of the following and otherwise die at POINT 1 with 're-run --from-phase d': final_backup.done exists; final_backup_gen is non-empty and equals stop_gen; 'test -s' on FINAL_BACKUP_FILE succeeds; the maintenance flag is present; and the camel-server container's '{{.Id}} {{.State.StartedAt}}', recorded by phase e right after the stop (for example as part of stop_gen), equals its current value, so any start since the stop invalidates the dump. In restore-ggf.sh, refuse *superseded* paths the same way as the gate dump, and optionally warn when the path is not the last final_backup_file in cutover-state vars. Add self-check mutation cases for (1)-(3). Update the checklist so --from-phase f is shown as valid only within the same stop window.
findings.defer_note: The fix goes into git-ignored host files, the same as P5-F1. It must land and be rehearsed in T18; it blocks T19. T18 must also show the docker ps guard aborting while camel-server is running, a positive test, because the self-check only greps for the guard string.
findings.resolution: Resolved (cycle 4 recovery confirm, hashes cutover-ggf.sh 85d785d251a2..., restore-ggf.sh af5c9d56761f...). Paths 1-3 die at failure point 1 before the snapshot. The first run does not false-fail. restore-ggf.sh refuses *superseded* dumps. Self-check has 77 checks, with mutation proofs. T18 must still show the running-server guard aborting on the real host (positive test).

findings.description: A re-run through phase e after the merge committed replaces the pre-merge restore point with a post-merge dump. final_backup and phase_e never consult merge.done or merge_started. Any --from-phase d or --from-phase e after merge.done takes the same route: a phase g failure, then a rebuild/retry, or the phase f running-server message 're-run with --from-phase d', which fires even after merge.done. That route records a new stop_gen, so final_backup sees final_backup_gen != stop_gen. It renames the true pre-merge final dump to *.superseded-<ts>, takes a fresh dump of the MERGED database and records it as final_backup_file. Phase f then skips the snapshot, merge and freshness guard because merge.done exists. Every later failure-point-2 recovery prints restore-ggf.sh with that post-merge dump. The restore succeeds, but it does not undo the merge, which contradicts the Rollback Plan ('DB from verified backup') and spec Appendix B.6. The only correct dump is now *superseded*, which this recovery's restore-ggf.sh change refuses with exit 2, so the scripted rollback cannot reach it. This was reproduced in a scratch harness that sources the real final_backup. The path is reachable through the documented '--from-phase <a-h>' mode (checklist runbook header), which is the same bar as P5-F5 paths 1-2.
findings.fix: In phase_e/final_backup, when merge_started or merge marker exists, never supersede or re-dump. Either die with a point-2 message ('merge committed: restore the recorded final dump, do not re-run phases d/e'), or keep final_backup_file unchanged and skip the dump. Make the phase f running-server message conditional: suggest '--from-phase d' only when merge.done is absent. After the merge, print the point-2 restore. Optionally have restore-ggf.sh warn when the given path is not the last final_backup_file in cutover-state vars. Add self-check cases: final_backup with the merge marker present makes no mv and no pg_dump, and the running-server message after merge.done does not suggest --from-phase d. Add a checklist line saying that --from-phase d/e is valid only before merge.done.

findings.resolution: Resolved within a single --date state dir (retry round 1 confirm, cutover-ggf.sh c96ecd3959b5..., restore-ggf.sh af5c9d56761f...). The central RESUME_POLICY/enforce_resume_policy runs before any phase. Defense in depth in final_backup/phase_e/phase_d and post-merge point-2 advice in phase f mean that, in PRE, IN-FLIGHT and POST, no --from-phase or plain resume can supersede or replace the pre-merge final dump once merge_started exists. 115 self-checks pass, and 7 mutation proofs each fail the self-check. The same consequence is still reachable across --date values; tracked separately as P5-F7.

findings.description: Merge state is scoped to --date, so the P5-F6 consequence is still reachable across dates. STATE_DIR, and with it every marker, the vars file and the resume policy's PRE/IN-FLIGHT/POST state, is cutover-state/<DATE_TAG>/. DATE_TAG defaults to today's UTC date, and the checklist's 'Run:' line and several printed resume hints ('continue from f, g or h', 'continue with --from-phase g') carry no --date. Suppose the merge commits under date X and phase g then fails or is interrupted, and the operator resumes on a later UTC day without --date, or with a mistyped date. The policy reads an empty dir and reports PRE. (1) '--from-phase g/h' dies at failure point 1 and prints 'Redeploy the OLD image (no DB restore needed)'. That is false after a committed merge: spec Appendix A.6 says the old image cannot run on the merged schema. (2) '--from-phase d' (or a plain run): phase a records the running container's image as old_image_id. If phase g had already run 'up -d', that is the NEW image, and phase c tags it camel-server:pre-merge-<Y>. Phase e then takes a fresh dump of the MERGED database and records it as backups/camel-pre-merge-<Y>-final-<ts>.dump, and the freshness guard passes because it is a fresh stop window. Phase f re-runs MERGE_CMD; the run-once guard in work-item-merge.sql prints 'copy skipped (no un-migrated tracker rows)' with rc 0, which validate_merge_output rejects at failure point 2 (the fx-skipped self-check case). print_recovery then names the post-merge dump. restore-ggf.sh accepts it, since it is neither superseded nor the gate dump, derives date Y from the file name and retags pre-merge-<Y>. So the restore undoes neither the merge nor the image. The real pre-merge dump and image tag still exist under date X, but nothing printed points to them. Reproduced in a stubbed-ssh harness that sources the real enforce_resume_policy and final_backup. This contradicts spec Appendix B.6 and the Rollback Plan, the same bar as P5-F6.
findings.fix: Constraint: the merge state, and the restore point it implies, must not depend on which --date dir is read. Options: (a) derive POST from the database itself before the phase loop (for example, any tracker_items row with migrated_to_id set, or no un-migrated rows), and die at point 2 when the DB says merged but this date's markers say PRE; (b) refuse to proceed when any other cutover-state/*/ dir holds merge_started.done or merge.done without a restore record. Pair this with P5-F3: restore-ggf.sh archives or marks cutover-state/<date>/ as restored, so a legitimate retry with a new --date after a restore still works. Also require an explicit --date for any --execute run whose state dir does not exist yet while another one does, or for any --from-phase run. Include '--date <X>' in every printed resume command and in the checklist 'Run:' line. Add self-check cases: another date dir in POST makes this date's run die at point 2 and never pg_dump; the DB-merged/markers-PRE mismatch dies.
findings.defer_note: The fix goes into git-ignored host files (not a correction commit). It must land and be rehearsed in T18, and it blocks T19. T18 should also rehearse a cross-midnight resume.
findings.resolution: Resolved in retry round 2 (content-hash audited). Merge state now comes from the DB first (tracker_items.migrated_to_id IS NOT NULL = MERGED), and that matches T7/T8 commit semantics exactly. A wrong, new or cross-midnight --date after a committed merge dies at point 2 before any phase: no old-image advice, no re-dump, no re-tag. Resumes need an explicit --date, and a restore archives its state dir. Residual: the printed restore command can name a dump from the wrong --date dir. That is tracked as P5-F9, not as a reopening of P5-F7.

findings.description: main reads final_backup_file and enforce_resume_policy reads the markers while POINT is still 0. When ssh fails there, the script correctly aborts, but print_recovery prints 'Aborted before any production change. Fix the cause and re-run', which is false when the host is actually in POST or IN-FLIGHT. Re-running is still safe because the policy then decides, so this is wording only.
findings.fix: Before reading host state, set the abort text to 'host state unknown (could not read cutover-state); do not act on the DB, re-run once ssh works', for example with a POINT value or a flag that print_recovery recognises.
findings.resolution: Resolved in retry round 2. print_recovery at POINT 0 says 'Aborted before any production change' only when SAFE_PRE=1 (known PRE and no phase-e marker); otherwise it says 'UNKNOWN or partly applied'. Host-state read failures set POINT=9 (UNKNOWN). The self-check covers both wordings.

findings.description: The point-2 restore command can name a stale dump from the wrong --date dir. main loads FINAL_BACKUP_FILE from cutover-state/<--date>/vars before enforce_resume_policy. In compute_merge_state's 'DB MERGED + no merge.done here' branch (the P5-F7 case), the die text correctly says to resume with the original --date or restore the final dump named in that dir. But POINT=2 print_recovery then prints 'bash deploy/restore-ggf.sh --execute ${FINAL_BACKUP_FILE}' with the value from the WRONG dir. Reachable without tampering: day 1, a default-date run (tag Y) aborts at point 1 after phase e (final dump recorded, merge markers absent or cleared after rc!=0) and is recovered (the site reopens). Day 2, a plain --execute gets tag X as a brand-new run; the cross-tag guard sees no merge markers in Y, so the run is PRE and the merge commits under X. Phase g fails, and the operator resumes with --date Y, for example copying the '--date Y --from-phase d' line from Y's point-1 advice. The printed restore names Y's day-1 dump, which predates the reopen and X's stop window. restore-ggf.sh accepts it (not superseded, not gate), retags pre-merge-Y and archives cutover-state/Y instead of X. All writes between Y's window and X's merge are lost: the P5-F1/F5/F6/F7 restore-point class, against spec Appendix B.6 and the Rollback Plan. Reproduced in a stubbed harness. The self-check case for this row sets FINAL_BACKUP_FILE=/b/pre.dump and asserts only the die text, so it does not catch this.
findings.fix: In the MERGED/no-merge.done branch, before die: set FINAL_BACKUP_FILE from final_backup_file in the vars of the single non-restored dir that holds merge.done (or merge_started). If that dir is not unique, or it is this dir with only merge_started, keep this dir's value only when this dir holds merge_started; otherwise blank it so print_recovery shows the placeholder. Optionally have restore-ggf.sh refuse a dump whose cutover-state/<date>/ has neither merge_started.done nor merge.done (unless --force-date is given). Add a self-check case: wrong-dir vars hold a final_backup_file, and the printed point-2 text must not contain it. Fix the wording for MERGED + merge_started-only in this dir, which currently says 'resume with the original --date (found: <this tag>)'; it should say the merge committed unrecorded and to restore this dir's final dump.

findings.resolution: Resolved (recovery confirm, cutover-ggf.sh f78e38e6aa3d...). compute_merge_state clears FINAL_BACKUP_FILE and sets it only from the marker dir. Other tag: that dir's dump. Same tag with merge_started only: this dir's dump plus 'committed but never recorded; do not resume'. Zero or several dirs: placeholder. The early load is removed. The full repro (Y aborts at point 1 and reopens, X merges, g fails, resume --date Y with no --from-phase and with a, d, e, f, g, h) now prints X's dump every time. findings.description: After restore-ggf.sh archives cutover-state/X as X.restored-<ts>, reusing --date X is not refused, even though the restore prints 'never reuse'. The DB is NOT_MERGED and X dir is absent, so the run is PRE. A plain run starts a fresh cutover under X: phase c keeps the existing pre-merge-X tag and dist, which are still the correct old ones. swap_dist_script, however, sees /var/www/camel.replaced-X from the first attempt (when its swap ran), skips the swap, and its cmp fails in phase g after the merge, forcing another point-2 restore. '--from-phase g' under X prints point-1 advice '--date X --from-phase d'; following it builds and loads the image and stops the server, then dies at point 1 in final_backup (no gate_backup_file). All paths fail safe.
findings.fix: check_date_policy: refuse a --date for which cutover-state/<date>.restored-* exists, telling the operator to use a new --date.
findings.resolution: Logic resolved (check_date_policy refuses a --date with <date>.restored-*; self-checked with stubbed rout; refusal confirmed in the patched harness). The implementation regresses every --execute run: see P5-F11. Close P5-F10 with the P5-F11 fix.

findings.description: The P5-F10 check in check_date_policy aborts every --execute run. Its remote string is rout "ls -d <remote>/cutover-state/$DATE_TAG.restored-* 2>/dev/null | head -n 1; true", and rout prefixes RPRE 'set -euo pipefail; '. When no archive matches, which is the normal state, ls exits non-zero on the literal glob (2 on GNU, 1 on BSD). pipefail carries that out of the pipeline, and errexit exits the remote shell before '; true'. ssh returns non-zero, so check_date_policy dies at POINT 9 with 'cannot check for a restored archive of <date>; failing closed'. That happens before enforce_resume_policy, phase a or any production change. This holds whatever the remote shell is: a shell without pipefail would fail RPRE itself on every remote command. Reach: every --execute, including the runbook's first run and every documented resume. log.json shows T18 and T19 WAITING, so no archive exists on the host. Fail-closed: no data or restore-point risk. But the T17 deliverable cannot perform a cutover, and every P5-F1/F5/F6/F7/F9 path is unreachable behind it. Missed by the 145-check gate because the self-check's run_dp stubs rout and never runs the remote string through a shell.
